task: Perform a focused security audit of the implemented academic rental property platform. Audit first, then propose fixes. Do not change files until the user approves the dry-run plan.
workflow: Inspect authentication, authorization, models, policies, middleware, controllers, Form Requests, API Resources, uploads, logging, CORS, Sanctum, environment examples, routes and tests.
Search source, config and Git history for secrets without exposing secret values in output.
Test object-level authorization and IDOR with two tenants and two landlords.
Test role separation for admin-only operations.
Inspect upload validation, storage isolation, image limits and featured-image behavior.
Inspect SQL injection, XSS, mass assignment, path traversal, CSRF, CORS and unsafe redirects.
Inspect rate limiting on authentication, password reset, uploads, contact requests, messaging and reports.
Inspect sensitive data in responses, logs and error messages.
Produce findings with severity, exact file/line, exploit scenario, evidence, fix, regression test and residual risk.
Propose 2-3 approaches for high-risk fixes and show tradeoffs.
Present exact files to change, dry-run diff plan, verification commands and rollback plan.
Stop and wait for approval before applying fixes.
After approval, fix critical/high findings in small cycles of no more than 20 files, add regression tests, rerun relevant tests and report exact outputs.
focus_areas: Visit request ownership and state transitions
constraints: Academic scope only. Do not add enterprise infrastructure.
No payment, SMS, AI/ML, government KYC, WebSockets or Redis.
Never modify node_modules, .git, dist or build.
Require explicit approval for migrations, deletion, dependency changes, destructive operations and production configuration.
Do not claim a finding is fixed without a passing regression test.
